extracted.intended_audience: general readers, media studies students, and television industry observers
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the defining features, scheduling conventions, regional variations, and programming strategies of late-night television (the daypart following prime time, roughly 11:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m.). Useful for describing or analyzing late-night TV formats and scheduling practices across markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late-night television time slot / definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Late-night television is one of the dayparts in television broadcast programming. It follows prime time and precedes the overnight television show graveyard slot. The slot generally runs from about 11:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m., with variations according to the time zone and broadcaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the canonical temporal bounds for identifying late-night programming and distinguishes it from prime time and the overnight 'graveyard' slot; note that exact hours vary by country, network, and local scheduling practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late-night television as synonymous with late-night talk show in the United States and Canada
rubrics_metrics.description: In the United States and Canada, the term is synonymous with the late-night talk show, a type of television comedy talk show and variety show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies that in North America the late-night programming block is often centered on comedy/variety talk shows and is considered an important programming block; this affects expectations for format, tone, and target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of a late-night news bulletin on major-network stations
rubrics_metrics.description: On most major-network stations, a late-night news bulletin airs at the beginning of the block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a common scheduling convention: networks often open the late-night block with a news summary before moving into entertainment programming. Producers and schedulers should account for this lead-in when planning placement and audience flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of time zones on scheduling and perceived East Coast bias in sports media
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the complications of effects of time zones on North American broadcasting, live professional sporting matches played in Pacific and Mountain Time Zone cities are often played in the primetime of those zones but late night in the Central and Eastern time zones, and their lateness often contributes to a perceived East Coast bias in sports media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-zone differences can make the same program 'late-night' in some regions and prime-time in others; this affects ratings, perceived regional bias, and scheduling strategies for live events (e.g., sports).

rubrics_metrics.name: United Kingdom late-night programming priorities and typical content
rubrics_metrics.description: In the United Kingdom, the late-night spot is from 11:00 p.m. to 12:30 a.m. and not seen as a priority; ITV, Channel 4 and Channel 5 air repeat programs in the time slot, and the BBC's channels primarily show BBC News, air movies, or repeats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UK broadcasters typically treat late-night as lower-priority filler time, favoring repeats, news, or movies rather than original late-night talk/variety formats common in North America; this informs expectations about original commissioning and audience investment in the slot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Australian and New Zealand late-night programming tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Australian and New Zealand television primarily air American late shows, lower-priority imported series, late movies or overflows of sports programming in the late-nighttime slot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These markets commonly rely on imported U.S. content and less-prioritized domestic programming for late-night hours; useful when assessing content origination and audience targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cable late-night strategies: timeshifts and rebranding to adult-oriented fare
rubrics_metrics.description: On cable television, programming strategies in this time slot include timeshifts of prime-time programs and, in the case of children's television channels, sign off and allowing more adult-oriented fare for the overnight hours under another brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cartoon Network switches to Adult Swim and Nickelodeon to Nick at Nite during late-night hours; these blocks typically air series programming (often reruns of sitcoms) with coarser language and more adult themes than daytime programming. Scheduling and branding shifts are common strategies to target different demographics overnight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Japan: late-night adult talk/variety shows and late-night anime
rubrics_metrics.description: After 11:00 p.m., Japan airs adult talk or variety shows as well as late-night anime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Japanese late-night scheduling favors adult-oriented variety/talk formats and anime targeted at older audiences; cultural/regulatory norms and audience habits shape content choices for the late-night window.
